summary: Step-by-step quickstart for streaming a packaged or Standalone Game UE app over a LAN: enable the Pixel Streaming plugin, add the -PixelStreamingURL launch flag, fetch the Pixel Streaming Infrastructure, start the Signalling Server and connect a browser.
gotchas: Plugin only works in a packaged app or when launched as Standalone Game, not PIE
Needs ports 80 and 8888 open and other web servers stopped
If the app window is minimized the input stream may stop; use -RenderOffScreen
Edit player page/config files in the original location, not the packaged copy, or they get overwritten

summary: Explains advanced Pixel Streaming deployment: STUN/TURN (ICE) servers for NAT traversal, multiple player pages per instance, on-demand scaling, and the experimental SFU for one-to-many simulcast streams.
gotchas: SFU feature is experimental
Matchmaker server deprecated in UE 5.5
Consumer NVIDIA GPUs often limit H.264 hardware encoding to eight sessions; Pixel Streaming 2 falls back to software encoders beyond the 8th
Self-hosted STUN/TURN IP and port must be visible on the open Internet

summary: Covers runtime hooks for Pixel Streaming: Freeze Frame/Unfreeze Frame Blueprint nodes, sending custom string/JSON responses to the player page, and binding Blueprint or C++ delegates for connection and stat events.
gotchas: Freezing the frame does not stop browser input being forwarded
OnDataTrackOpen, OnDataTrackClose and OnFallbacktoSoftwareEncoding are Pixel Streaming 2 only

summary: Conceptual overview of Pixel Streaming: rendering a UE app on a remote machine and streaming encoded frames/audio over WebRTC to browsers, with the plugin and Signalling and Web Server components and the connection sequence.

Migration notes for moving from the original Pixel Streaming plugin to Pixel Streaming 2 (new WebRTC layer, renamed Blueprint nodes, changed C++ API and settings), plus steps to receive a stream in-engine with a Pixel Streaming Peer component and Media Texture.
gotchas: Blueprint nodes must be manually recreated when migrating; no redirector is possible
C++ API removed all WebRTC types
Settings priority: .ini overridden by command line, overridden by console
Use the Pixel Streaming Infrastructure branch matching your engine version

summary: Describes the externally hosted Pixel Streaming Infrastructure GitHub repo (Frontend, SignallingWebServer, SFU, Matchmaker), how to get it via ZIP, git clone or the get_ps_servers script, and the need to match branch to engine version.
gotchas: Matchmaker deprecated from UE 5.5
Must use the infrastructure branch matching your engine version; master is experimental
Using get_ps_servers places the servers where they are packaged automatically with the project

summary: Walkthrough of the Pixel Streaming Demo sample from Fab: the showcase.html player page, how emitUIInteraction JSON events reach the Orbit_Controller Blueprint via OnPixelStreamingInputEvent, and the in-game widget demoing freeze frame, audio, video and player components.
gotchas: Infrastructure version must match the engine version
Sample only appears in Fab Library when a compatible engine version is installed

summary: Guide to trading off image quality, latency and resiliency in Pixel Streaming via encoder Quality bounds, bitrate, keyframe/intra-refresh, coupled vs decoupled framerate, with recommended starting settings for one-to-one 1080p streams.
gotchas: Old QP parameter (lower = better) replaced by Quality (higher = better) in 5.5
Decoupled mode adds 1-2 frames of latency in all cases
NVENC intra-refresh options are NVIDIA-only and removed in Pixel Streaming 2
Active RDP connections on the host can badly drop FPS

summary: Reference of Pixel Streaming requirements and settings: supported GPUs/encoders (NVENC, AMF, VideoToolbox; H.264, VP8, VP9, AV1), default ports, required launch args, and console variables for plugin, encoder and WebRTC configuration.
gotchas: Error 'No compatible GPU found' means GPU lacks NVENC, AMF or VideoToolbox
AV1 needs NVIDIA Ada Lovelace or newer
Only tested on Windows 10/11, specific Ubuntu versions and macOS Ventura 13.5.1
Many settings changed or were removed in Pixel Streaming 2

summary: Overview of UAT BuildCookRun stages (build, cook, stage, package, deploy, run) and the three ways to package: the Platforms toolbar menu, Project Launcher custom profiles, or RunUAT on the command line; also explains cook by the book vs cook on the fly and deploy modes.
gotchas: Hand-authored UAT command lines are error-prone; copy the one a Custom Launch Profile prints in the Output Log
In UE 5.4.0 'Use Project Setting' build configuration only took the value from editor startup (fixed in 5.4.1)
Greyed-out platform usually means missing/unsupported SDK
Cook on the fly without -filehostip loads local files instead of the Cook Server

summary: Reference for the Device Manager window (Platforms > Device Manager): adding unlisted devices by identifier, claiming/releasing/sharing, connecting, remote power on/off/reboot, viewing device details and feature compatibility, and terminating running processes.
gotchas: Devices outside the LAN need a stable IP address
The feature compatibility list is not exhaustive

summary: Explains splitting cooked content into numbered chunks (.pak files) using Primary Asset Rules in Project Settings > Asset Manager, DefaultGame.ini PrimaryAssetRules overrides, or PrimaryAssetLabel data assets, and auditing chunk contents with Asset Audit, Size Map and Reference Viewer.
gotchas: Assets with no or negative chunk ID go into chunk 0
.pak files are platform-specific and not interchangeable
Size Map memory mode shows editor memory, which can differ greatly from shipped disk size

summary: Command-line reference for the Cook commandlet (UnrealEditor.exe -run=cook) with its full option table: target platforms, iterative cooks, map selection, cook-on-the-fly server mode, DLC options and validation flags.
gotchas: Without -iterate the sandbox directory is deleted and everything recooked
-NoGameAlwaysCook, -NoDefaultMaps, -CookSkipRequests and -SkipSoftReferences likely produce cooks missing content
-SkipHardReferences is only for debugging

summary: Deep C++ reference for how classes interact with the cooker: declaring or suppressing runtime references, transforming data in Serialize/PreSave/BeginCacheForCookedPlatformData, stripping objects per platform, declaring build dependencies and version bumps for incremental cooks, and AssetManager chunk assignment.
gotchas: IsCachedCookedPlatformDataLoaded must eventually return true or the cooker soft-locks
Do not cache GConfig reads in statics; hidden config dependencies cause false positive incremental skips
Native cook code changes need a version bump (UPROPERTY change, CustomVersion or AppendToClassSchema guid)
Cooking directly in the editor process is not supported; the cooker is always a separate process

summary: Hub page for XR UI: links to pages on 3D widgets, attaching items to the HMD, visualizing play area bounds, OpenXR stereo layers and OpenXR loading screens.

Hub for handheld AR development linking the Handheld AR Template pages and supported devices, with a table of AR features (plane detection, occlusion, environment probes, ARPins, augmented images, face tracking, geotracking, camera intrinsics) and their ARCore/ARKit support.
gotchas: OpenXR cannot be used for handheld AR devices
People Occlusion and Geotracking are ARKit-only

summary: Overview of OpenXR for head-mounted AR/VR in UE: runtimes, XR plugin priority order, bundled OpenXR extension plugins, and internally vs externally validated headsets on Windows and Android.
gotchas: OpenXR in UE supports only head-mounted devices
Plugin priority: Oculus > OpenXR > Windows Mixed Reality > SteamVR; first runtime that connects wins
Epic does not support device-specific features on externally validated devices

summary: Hub page listing Android guides: Google Play achievements and leaderboards, AdMob ads, manifest control, in-app purchases, virtual keyboard, Android development reference, Vulkan mobile renderer and launch screens.
Hub page for mobile development tools linking the Mobile Previewer, Unreal Plugin Language (UPL) and mobile performance guidelines.
Hub page for starting XR projects: links to new AR project setup, the VR Template, Handheld AR Template pages, XR best practices, and follow-on XR input, UI, sharing and profiling guides.

Explains one-click launch of the current level to a device via the Platforms toolbar drop-down (cook, install, run), the generic UnrealGame executable used for content-only projects, and where to find Unreal Frontend for advanced cook/deploy options.
gotchas: One-click launch only installs the current level; switching levels is unsupported
Content-only projects show as 'UnrealGame' when one-click deployed; packaged builds use the project name

summary: Explains low-latency frame syncing: choosing whether the game thread syncs to the render thread, RHI thread or swap-chain present (r.GTSyncType) and tuning rhi.SyncSlackMS to trade input latency against hitch resilience.
gotchas: Lower rhi.SyncSlackMS reduces latency but makes hitches more likely to drop frames
r.GTSyncType 2 falls back to mode 1 on unsupported platforms
Benefit is smaller at 60 Hz than at 30 Hz

summary: Hub page for XR input: OpenXR interaction profiles, Motion Controller Component setup and usage pages, and Oculus Quest hand tracking via the Oculus VR plugin.
gotchas: Hand tracking on Oculus Quest cannot be used with an OpenXR project

summary: Hub page on mobile platform services (achievements, leaderboards, ads, in-app purchases, local notifications) wired through plugins and the Unreal Plugin Language, linking each guide.
Hub page linking Android optimization guides: bundled PSO caches, Unreal Insights on Android devices, and reducing Android binary size.

Hub page for mobile performance: links to mobile performance guidelines, Unreal Insights on Android, Oodle, PSO caches, mesh auto-instancing, Android device profiles/scalability, Animation Budget Allocator and the Android Configuration Rules System.

Hub page for Pixel Streaming (streaming a remote UE app's frames and audio to browsers via WebRTC with keyboard, mouse, touch, gamepad/XR and custom HTML input), linking overview, getting started, hosting, editor streaming, tuning, Pixel Streaming 2, reference, infrastructure and sample pages.
gotchas: Pixel Streaming in Editor is experimental

summary: Step-by-step Project Launcher custom profile for a versioned Shipping release on Windows: Shipping build, cook by the book, 'Create a release version' with version number, compress/unversioned/UnrealPak options, package and store locally, and where the release asset registry and pak end up.
keys: Create a release version of the game for distribution.
Store all content in a single file (UnrealPak)
gotchas: Keep the asset registry and pak from Releases\[Version]\[Platform]; they are needed for future patches or DLC
Release versioning is still recommended when distributing via Steam

summary: Shows how to set per-device CVars and LOD settings in Config/DefaultDeviceProfiles.ini (with iOS r.MobileContentScaleFactor and Android profile selectors) and how to use Platform Memory Buckets to vary settings like r.Streaming.PoolSize and TextureLODGroups by device RAM.
gotchas: r.MobileContentScaleFactor is relative to the device's nominal iOS resolution, not its actual resolution

summary: Explains Title and Action safe zones and how to show a debug overlay for them with r.DebugSafeZone console variables (mode, ratio, overlay alpha) via the console or DefaultEngine.ini [SystemSettings], to keep UI away from screen edges.
gotchas: Must run in Windowed Fullscreen or Fullscreen or the zone displays at the wrong size
Title and Action zones cannot both be shown at once
UI may not update when ratios change at runtime; switch game modes to see changes

summary: Hub page for multi-user XR: links to ARPins, the VR Spectator Screen and the Collab Viewer templates.

Lists XR devices verified with UE and their SDK versions: ARCore 1.37 Android and ARKit 4.0 iOS handhelds, Meta Quest 2/3, Apple Vision Pro, HTC Vive/Vive Pro, Valve Index, PSVR/PSVR2, with links to ARCore and ARKit pages.
gotchas: HTC Vive has minimal support
Android handheld AR requires Android 7.0+, iOS requires iOS 11.0+

summary: Explains the Beta Multi-Process Cook (director plus local worker processes) to cut cook times on large projects, enabled via [CookSettings] CookProcessCount or -cookprocesscount, with memory tuning settings and troubleshooting of worker errors.
gotchas: Beta feature; use caution when shipping
In UE 5.4 it could report success on a failed cook (fixed in 5.4.3)
Unlikely to help small projects like Lyra; uses more RAM
Workers only run on the local machine; World Partition levels cause repeated retraction failures

summary: Reference for AutoSDK, a source-controlled folder layout of platform SDKs that UnrealBuildTool switches between on demand via the UE_SDKS_ROOT environment variable and per-version Setup.bat/Unsetup.bat scripts.
gotchas: Epic cannot distribute SDKs; the shipped folder is only a template and must not be used directly
Submit the AutoSDK folder to source control separately from game/engine code

summary: Full reference for the Project Launcher (Platforms > Project Launcher): default vs custom launch profiles and every setting in the Build, Cook (by the book / on the fly, release/DLC/patch, pak and chunk options), Package (I/O Store, prerequisites installer), Archive, Deploy and Launch sections.
keys: Iterative Cooking: Only cook content modified from previous cook
Store all content in a single file (UnrealPak)
Use container files for optimized loading (I/O Store)
Include an installer for prerequisitea of packaged games
gotchas: Shipping strips console commands, stats and profiling tools
Save Packages Without Versions is described as potentially dangerous
DLC without Include Engine Content errors when accessing Engine content
File Server 'Streaming server' option is experimental

summary: Describes UnrealFrontend (standalone exe or editor tab) for building, cooking, deploying and launching builds, browsing devices and running sessions, viewing remote logs and sending console commands via Session Console, and running automation tests on session instances.
gotchas: Source-build users must build UnrealFrontend in Visual Studio or Xcode first
Session Console only shows log output since the session was discovered
Unreal Remote Agent is currently not supported
Launcher supports only a limited set of cook/deploy options (cook on the fly, file server, deploy to local Windows)

summary: Explains building game targets for Windows on ARM64 (native ARM64, ARM64EC, or combined arm64+x64 builds) via Platforms > Package Project > Windows architecture choice or RunUAT BuildCookRun -clientarchitecture, plus GDK support.
gotchas: Experimental feature
Game targets only; ARM64/ARM64EC editor builds are not supported
Clang is not supported for ARM64 targets; use MSVC
Combined builds require the command line; GDK support needs the April 2026 GDK or later

summary: Explains how to use cooked (Windows) assets inside the editor: required DefaultEngine.ini settings, copying .uasset/.uexp/.ubulk files from Saved\Cooked, and the read-only behaviour and asset-type limitations of cooked content.
keys: Allow Cooked Content in the Editor
gotchas: Windows platform content only
Cooked assets are read-only, cannot be opened in editors, moved or renamed; keep the original folder structure
Known issues with cooked Niagara and Blueprints
Deleting a cooked asset may leave its .uexp/.ubulk files behind

summary: Hub page for ARPins (fixed real-world AR anchor locations), linking the ARPin Local Storage Quick Start and ARPin Overview.

keys: Set Spectator Screen Mode Texture Plus Eye Layout
gotchas: Not expected on mobile VR; enabled by default except on PS VR
Distorted mode is Oculus-only

SceneCapture for the spectator texture can be expensive; capture at ~30 fps

summary: Requirements and starting links for Google ARCore handheld AR on Android: Codeworks for Android, Android version 26+, a connected device and the Google ARCore plugin, plus links to the Handheld AR Template, ARPins and profiling guides.
gotchas: Requires Android version 26 or greater and a supported connected device

summary: Requirements and links for Apple ARKit handheld AR on iOS: Xcode 12+, iOS 14+, an A12 Bionic or newer device and the Apple ARKit plugin, with profiling links and known limitations.
gotchas: Needs a device with an A12 Bionic chip or greater
Image-detection candidate images must have unique friendly names or only the first is recognized

summary: Hub page for packaging and platform delivery: links to build operations, cooking, chunking, launching to devices, multi-process cooking, release versioning, Project Launcher, Unreal Frontend, C++ cooking reference, AutoSDK, Device Manager, device profiles, and mobile, Android, iOS, XR and Pixel Streaming sections.

Introduces the Lyra Starter Game sample: how to get it from Fab or for source builds, its game mode maps and content paths, World Partition cell loading, and its Game Feature Plugin and LyraExperienceDefinition architecture, with links to Lyra subsystem pages (abilities, animation, input, inventory, scalability).

World Partition maps like Expanse open empty until you load grid cells

keys: Set Spectator Screen Mode Texture Plus Eye Layout

Notes on interpreting VR profiling data: false-positive occlusion/scene traversal spikes, compositor-induced 90/45 Hz framerate stepping, and emulating stereo rendering on desktop with -emulatestereo to profile without that effect.
gotchas: The VR compositor acts like vsync, so missing framerate drops to 90/n Hz and causes sudden-looking drops

summary: Lists external VR profiling tools for UE: Oculus Performance HUD via OculusDebugTool.exe, the SteamVR Frame Timing tool, and RenderDoc frame capture with ToggleDrawEvents.
